name: Bio-Inspired Computing
description: Test your knowledge of the main concepts, techniques, and applications of bio-inspired computing.

questions.question: What is the main motivation behind the development of Bio-Inspired Computing?
options: Completely replace the use of traditional hardware in systems.
Model computational systems based on effective solutions found in nature.
Guarantee the deterministic execution of any complex algorithm.
Reduce the electrical consumption of computers to nearly zero.
questions.explain: Bio-inspired computing investigates techniques inspired by biology to build adaptive systems based on nature.

questions.question: What are the three fundamental steps in designing an Artificial Neural Network?
options: Hardware definition, language choice, and final testing.
Sample selection, data cleaning, and report creation.
Definition of the artificial neuron, network structure, and learning.
Input collection, code compilation, and graphical analysis.
questions.explain: The design requires defining the artificial neuron, the connection architecture, and the weight-adjustment method.

questions.question: What is the main objective of weight adjustment during Neural Network training?
options: Minimize the cost function calculated from the errors made.
Increase the clock speed of the system's processors.
Eliminate the need for activation functions in hidden layers.
Reduce the amount of data required in the training set.
questions.explain: The algorithm adjusts the weights proportionally to the error to minimize the cost function over time.

questions.question: What characterizes the property of Emergent Intelligence in bio-inspired systems?
options: A centralized agent making all decisions for the group.
Complex capabilities arising from the interaction between simple agents.
Pre-programmed instructions executed in isolation by robots.
Exclusive use of centralized high-speed memory.
questions.explain: Emergent intelligence occurs when complex global behaviors arise from the self-organization of simple agents without central control.

questions.question: How do ant colony-based algorithms find the shortest path?
options: Through an exhaustive scan of all possible routes in the graph.
By depositing markers that intensify on the most traveled routes.
By directly calculating distances using GPS coordinates.
Only with random movement and no route memory retention.
questions.explain: Ants chemically reinforce the most frequent routes, allowing the colony to converge on the shortest path.

questions.question: In Evolutionary Computation, which element acts as the Natural Selection criterion?
options: The rate of bit variation present in main memory.
The number of iterations of the main loop.
The Fitness Function that measures the fitness of individuals.
The predetermined maximum size of the initial population.
questions.explain: The fitness function determines which individuals are best suited to pass their genetic material to the next generations.

questions.question: What is the function of the Mutation operator in a Genetic Algorithm?
options: Guarantee immediate convergence to a single local solution.
Evaluate the quality of the solution found by the individual.
Introduce random perturbations to maintain diversity.
Remove the worst individuals from the population each generation.
questions.explain: Mutation inserts small random changes, allowing exploration of new areas of the search space and preventing stagnation.

questions.question: What does the field of Artificial Life study within the context of Bio-Inspired Computing?
options: The creation of biological organs using three-dimensional printers.
The recreation of biological phenomena and logic in virtual environments.
The automation of human DNA sequencing.
The replacement of biological neurons with integrated circuits.
questions.explain: Artificial Life applies biological rules in software and virtual worlds to simulate the behavior of living beings.

questions.question: What is the main objective of systems based on Autonomic Computing?
options: Function without needing a connection to external networks.
Perform self-management and self-adjustment without human intervention.
Train artificial intelligence models without using data.
Replace all operating systems with genetic code.
questions.explain: Inspired by the autonomic nervous system, autonomic computing seeks to create systems that self-regulate and adapt on their own.

questions.question: In Bio-Inspired Robotics, what is the advantage of using a joint structure similar to that of a spider or centipede?
options: Greater stability and adaptability on uneven terrain.
A drastic decrease in the manufacturing cost of mechanical components.
Elimination of sensors for navigation and obstacle detection.
An increase in final movement speed on flat surfaces.
questions.explain: Articulated locomotion inspired by insects and arachnids improves stability and mobility on rough terrain.
